name: rough-annotation
title: Rough Annotation
description: Hand-drawn marks around any text or element: underline, box, circle, highlight, strike-through, crossed-off and bracket, drawn stroke by stroke, with a group that plays them in order.
label: Rough Notation by Preet Shihn
author: Preet Shihn <https://github.com/pshihn>
attribution: Rough Notation, Copyright (c) 2020 Preet Shihn. MIT License.

props.name: type
props.description: Required. The mark. It cannot change on a live annotation: a new type draws a new one.

props.name: show
props.description: Draw the mark. Turning it off hides it at once; turning it on again animates it. Ignored inside a RoughNotationGroup.

props.name: animate
props.description: Draw stroke by stroke. Under prefers-reduced-motion the mark always appears at once.

props.name: animationDuration
props.description: Milliseconds to draw the whole mark (shared between the lines of a multiline mark and by length between its strokes).

props.name: color
props.description: Any CSS color, including var(--token). The highlight type defaults to the --rough-annotation-highlight token instead, because a text-colored bar would hide the text.

props.name: strokeWidth
props.description: Stroke width in pixels. Default 2; highlight ignores it and uses 95% of the line height.

props.name: padding
props.description: Space between the content and the mark in pixels: one value, [vertical, horizontal] or [top, right, bottom, left].

props.name: iterations
props.description: Passes of the pen. Underline, strike-through, crossed-off and highlight alternate direction on each pass; a circle draws a double outline for every two iterations.

props.name: multiline
props.description: Annotate each line of wrapped inline text separately instead of one box around all of it.

props.name: brackets
props.description: Which sides a bracket mark covers. `start` and `end` follow the text direction (`end` is the right in left-to-right text, the left in right-to-left); `left` and `right` are physical. Upstream's default is the right side.

props.name: rtl
props.description: Start drawing from the right. Default: the element's computed direction, read when the annotation is created, so Arabic and Hebrew text is drawn from its start.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render. Use a block element (p, blockquote) for a bracket, and a semantic one (mark, del, ins, em, strong) when the mark carries meaning.

props.name: RoughNotationGroup show
props.description: Wrap several RoughNotation elements to draw them one after another in document order. Their own show props are ignored.

a11y: The marks are decoration: every annotation is an SVG with aria-hidden="true" and pointer events off, so it adds nothing to the accessibility tree and never takes a click. Meaning belongs in the markup: render a strike-through as `del`, a highlight as `mark`, an emphasis as `em` or `strong` (the `as` prop; the component clears the browser's own yellow `mark` fill and `del` line so the hand-drawn mark is not doubled).
Under prefers-reduced-motion the marks are drawn at once, with no stroke animation, including a mark that was mid-draw when the preference switched on.

Right to left: a line mark (underline, strike-through, crossed-off, highlight) starts drawing from the right when the text's computed direction is rtl (read when the annotation is created; the `rtl` prop overrides it). Positions are measured from the rendered text, so boxes, circles and brackets follow mirrored layouts, and a bracket's default side `end` is the left in right-to-left text.

Contrast (fidelity default, contrast on request): the default highlight tokens already keep body text above 4.5:1 (measured 16.0:1 in light, 8.1:1 in dark, against `--card`). Under prefers-contrast: more the bar switches to `--rough-annotation-highlight-contrast`, a stronger amber that reads as a shape (3.2:1 in light, 3.5:1 in dark against the card) while text on it keeps 6.2:1 and 5.1:1. Under forced colors the highlight bar becomes the system `Mark` color with `MarkText` text, and every other mark takes the system text color (`CanvasText`), because the shape, not its color, carries the meaning.
The color you pass is yours: give text-colored marks (underline, box, circle) at least 3:1 against the page, and never rely on a mark's color alone to say what it means.
